prompt:
Use the attached ORIGINAL ASHVEIL ASH CROW atlas only for the SAME bird identity, proportions, black pointed beak, small dark eyes, charcoal feather layers, tiny blue-grey highlights and detailed crisp pixel clusters. Draw NEW poses, not relabelled idle frames. One head, exactly TWO articulated feathered wings, exactly TWO scaly legs with taloned feet, short wedge/fan tail. No human arms, no extra legs or wings, no bat membranes, messenger tube, red thread, gear, glow, effects or gore.

Transparent RGBA PNG atlas, EXACTLY 4 rows x 4 columns, 16 wholly separated birds. Row1 FRONT faces toward bottom/viewer; row2 LEFT beak to left edge; row3 RIGHT beak to right edge; row4 BACK faces away toward top, beak hidden and tail toward viewer. Keep one consistent elevated 3/4 game camera and same body/head size. Each whole silhouette stays in central 55-60 percent of its cell, with large empty transparent gutters and no touching neighbors or canvas edge. No text, grid, labels, backdrop, checkerboard, shadows, ground, scenery or border. Keep a stable virtual ground-projection baseline per row, including airborne poses. No huge body scaling between frames.

Draw a natural CROW PECK attack in four unmistakably distinct keyframes, targeting empty space near the ground: 1 ANTICIPATION body crouches, neck draws back and head is raised slightly, two feet firmly planted, wings folded; 2 PECK CONTACT head and neck dart LOW/FORWARD along facing direction, beak tip points toward ground ahead, breast shifts forward and tail tilts up; 3 FOLLOW THROUGH lowest neck/head position with beak almost touching virtual ground, feet remain braced and wings may loosen slightly for balance; 4 RECOVERY neck retracts and head returns upright, tail settles, wings fully fold. The actual beak and head must visibly travel, NOT a wing attack, NOT merely four standing crow head tilts. No depicted victim/corpse/body/food/eye/blood, no impact effects; show the bird only. Back-facing row pecks away from the viewer so the head drops behind its far side and tail raises toward viewer; do not turn it to face the viewer. Both wings and the two-legged support structure remain credible throughout.
